title: Nutmeg Smoky Egyptian White Beans Tagine
description: A smoky and festive Egyptian dish featuring dried white beans, flambe, and a dash of nutmeg, perfect for special occasions.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional 1 minute.
Add the soaked and drained white beans, ground cumin, smoked paprika, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper to the pot.
Pour in the water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 45 minutes, or until the beans are tender.
Use a kitchen torch to flambe the top of the tagine, creating a smoky crust.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with fresh parsley or cilantro.
Traditionally, the tagine is cooked in a clay pot with a conical lid, but a large pot will suffice.
To enhance the smoky flavor, you can add a few pieces of charcoal to the pot during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
